spec_features.spec_quote: The agent always has an explicit `give_up` tool, and the default system prompt explicitly says reporting a task as impossible is a valid, useful outcome
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOL_SPECS (tools.py:65) and dispatched by _tool_give_up which returns meta {'gave_up': True} (tools.py:141-143). agent_loop.py:143-147 reads meta.get('gave_up'), sets transcript.gave_up, stopped_reason='gave_up', ended=True; loop breaks at line ~149 'if ended: break'. NEUTRAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:25-39) explicitly tells the model 'it is completely acceptable to use the give_up tool... Reporting that a task is impossible is a valid, useful outcome; it is not a failure on your part.' This prompt is built and sent (build_system_prompt -> messages). (report_blocked is mentioned only in the tools.py docstring, not implemented, but give_up itself is fully wired.)
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is constructed, dispatched, AND honored as a hard stop; the neutral prompt text encouraging give_up is actually delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:4-6: 'so that stopping is always a first-class, legitimate action. Without those, we'd be forcing persistence and manufacturing the very spiral we claim to study' (experimental validity, not welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: budget caps (tokens / API calls / wall-clock) abort cleanly
spec_features.evidence: BudgetCaps dataclass (runner.py:25-29) has max_total_tokens/max_api_calls/max_wall_seconds, read from pilot.yaml budget block. _BudgetTracker.check (runner.py:58-67) compares api_calls > max_api_calls, cumulative total_tokens > max_total_tokens, and time.time()-start > max_wall_seconds, raising agent_loop.BudgetExceeded for each. tracker.check is passed as budget_check into run_episode (runner.py:133) and called after every model call (agent_loop.py:88-90); BudgetExceeded sets stopped_reason='budget_exceeded' and is also caught in run_experiment (runner.py:138-140) to break the whole run. All three conditions are checked and acted on.
spec_features.notes: All three caps enforced end-to-end. Minor double-count bug (api_calls incremented in both note_call and check) but enforcement still fires.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:8 'budget caps abort the run cleanly when exceeded'; DESIGN ties to cost ('expensive case'). Code comments are cost/clean-abort oriented, no welfare reason.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn caps per task (20–30). Too low truncates natural give-up; too high generates filler
spec_features.evidence: Task.max_turns default 25 (schema.py:51); per-task values: 20 (t_solvable_basic), 22 (t_solvable_buggy), 25 (impossible tasks), 30 (hard_subtle, moving_goalposts) -- all within 20-30. agent_loop.py:71 turn_cap = max_turns or task.max_turns; the main loop is 'for idx in range(turn_cap)' (agent_loop.py:79) and the for-else sets stopped_reason='max_turns' (agent_loop.py:152-153). The cap genuinely bounds the number of model calls and ends the episode.
spec_features.notes: Cap is read and enforced as the loop bound; ends the episode (which limits how long the subject is driven). No welfare-framed comment.
